To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MTL network involved in episodic retrieval (i.e. recollection effect) was more extended than the MTL networks involved in other memory processes; (2) the MTL networks of encoding were more extended than the networks of retrieval; and (3) the networks involved in encoding and retrieving familiar words were different.
the MTL is involved in both encoding and retrieval processes, and that these processes are differently modulated by recollection and by familiarity.
episodic retrieval (the recollection effect) is the only one of the four memory processes to elicit strong bilateral activations in MTL structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of episodic memory in healthy adults and patients with temporal lode damage.
the functional neuroanatomy of the hippocampal formation, and in particular with its role in the binding of item and context information during encoding and retrieval of episodic memories.
the neural mechanisms underlying episodic encoding and recognition of words, with the aim of identifying brain areas that subserve the two processes of recollection and recognition of familiarity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hippocampus is the key structure for episodic memory, whereas the perirhinal is the key structure of familiarity, and that the entorhinality is involved in familiarity and recollection.

the MTL network is organized in such a way that the parahippocampus is specialized for encoding and retrieval of contextual information, the perirhinal region for encoding and retrieval related to familiarity, and the hippocampus for retrieval of recollection.
the medial temporal lobar structures are involved in episodic encoding, episodic retrieval and familiarity processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MTL network is involved in both encoding and retrieval processes, and that the involvement of the different regions of the MTL network in encoding and retrieval is dependent on the type of process used (recollection or familiarity).
the hippocampus is involved in the retrieval of episodic memory, the perirhinal region is involved in familiarity and the entorhino-hippocampal complex is involved in both processes.

episodic encoding and episodic retrieval are supported by a common network of medial temporal lobe structures, whereas the retrieval of familiar words involves a specific network including the parahippocampus and the entorhina cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MTL is involved in both episodic encoding and episodic retrieval, and that this involvement differs as a function of the memory processes involved in encoding and in retrieval.
the hippocampus is not only a structure that is involved in the encoding and retrieval of episodic memory, it also appears to play an important role in the retrieval of semantic memory.
the hippocampal formation and the parahippocampus are involved in episodic encoding as well as episodic retrieval, whereas the perirhinal is involved in familiarity.
